about: Kogaki's settings for non-coding operation (kogaki#1307). Change a value here and the next run uses it; no code change and no Issue are needed. Every key below is required: a run that needs a key this file does not carry refuses, naming the key. Terrain's own values still live in src/terrain-workflow.json.

brief.call_limit_s_means: How long, in seconds, one call of a Brief job unit may run before it is stopped and asked again. A compose job unit makes two calls per attempt (it composes one Candidate, then has its Move fit judged); a path-review unit makes one. A stopped call uses up one attempt.
brief.unit_attempts_means: How many attempts each Brief job unit gets. A refused answer or a stopped call uses one; an answer that is not readable at all is asked again without using one. There is no limit on the whole job. Its longest run is this number, times the calls per attempt plus this number again (an unreadable answer is asked again up to this many times per attempt, each a full call), times call_limit_s: with 3 attempts, 2 calls and 900 s, a compose job unit can run 3 x 5 x 900 s, about 3 hours and 45 minutes, though a normal attempt takes 10 to 15 minutes.
brief.compose_units_means: How many Candidates the compose job asks for at once, one job unit each.
brief.judge_model_means: The model every Brief judgment and every job unit is asked with.
brief.audience_file_means: The Audience file the Brief composes for. Its `persona` key says who the reader is and what they already know; its `register` key says how the prose addresses them.
